passages.text:
[Canadian 24-Hour Movement Guidelines for Adults aged 18-64 > 24-Hour Movement Guidelines (adults 18-64) - summary]
- Move more: at least 150 minutes per week of moderate-to-vigorous aerobic physical activity; muscle-strengthening activities at least twice per week; several hours of light physical activity including standing. - Reduce sedentary time: 8 hours or less of sedentary time per day, including no more than 3 hours of recreational screen time, and break up long periods of sitting. - Sleep well: 7 to 9 hours of good-quality sleep on a regular basis, with consistent bed and wake times. - Some activity is better than none; progress gradually.

passages.text:
[Overweight and obesity are rising in Canada (Canadian Health Measures Survey 2022-2024) > Measured obesity in Canadian adults > Key findings]
- Among adults aged 18 to 79, measured obesity prevalence rose from 25% in 2016-2019 (pre-pandemic) to 33% in 2022-2024. - Prevalence was highest among adults aged 40 to 59 (38% of males, 35% of females). Among adults 60 to 79 it was 35% of males and 33% of females. - The largest increase was among young adults aged 18 to 39, starting from 22% before the pandemic. - Statistics Canada notes that pandemic-related lifestyle changes such as reduced physical activity and more sedentary time may have contributed.

The Edmonton Obesity Staging System considers metabolic, physical and psychological parameters. - Care follows a patient journey framework that begins with asking permission to discuss weight (the 5As approach starts with ASK). - Treatment pillars include medical nutrition therapy, physical activity, psychological interventions, pharmacotherapy and bariatric surgery, chosen with a clinician.
